notes: Correct AST-based fix with a tidy slices.ContainsFunc helper and extensive tests (raw/triple-quoted strings, latency, dynamic names), though it renames and replaces existing tests such as TestTransportErrorPlaceholder, adding some churn.

Same approach as the reference, cleanly done with slices.ContainsFunc; integration tests cover every response placeholder (including latency) in both shorthand and direct ph() form, though the hostport-gating trick in the response test is a bit convoluted.

Works and handles dynamic and literal names correctly, but it puts reverse-proxy-specific placeholder knowledge (isResponsePlaceholder, ReferencesResponseData) into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, and its integration tests cover only one request-only case.

Behaviour is correct, but it puts the reverse_proxy-specific placeholder list inside the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, a layering leak, and its updated comments wrongly imply response expressions are not evaluated on transport errors; only one integration test was added.

Functionally equivalent to the reference with a clean generic MayUsePlaceholder API; its tests are the most complete, covering both shorthand and ph() for every placeholder, mixed request-only and response sets, and that request-only expressions still gate transport-error retries.

Collects literal placeholder names and a dynamic-name flag from the checked CEL AST, then matches them against an exact response-placeholder list in reverseproxy, which mirrors the reference; tests cover request-only, look-alike, escaped, dynamic and transport-error cases at both the unit and integration level.

Same AST-based approach as the reference: it records literal placeholder names plus a dynamic-name flag at provision time and checks them with a reverse-proxy-local predicate, backed by thorough table tests for shorthand, ph(), near-miss names, escaped literals and POST-body preservation.

Equivalent to the reference, with a generic ReferencesPlaceholder predicate in caddyhttp and the response-placeholder classification kept in reverseproxy; thorough unit tests on near-miss names, plus GET/POST integration tests checking that body and headers are preserved.
